1.say: This sentence can be read two ways. 'Both ministers could sign it.' Either each of them is allowed to, or the two of them together are able to. Which did you mean? The first. Then write 'either minister may sign it'. In a report an ambiguity is a fault. Sarah has one in her review on purpose. 'A book about a man who cannot be trusted with a story.' And you cannot tell whether it is the man or the author who is not to be trusted. She meant both. Then it is a tool and not a fault. The test is whether the writer chose it. There is a question in the ministry's letter that I cannot answer. 'When did the district stop checking the figures?' Answer it and you have agreed that they stopped. I had not noticed that. Every question carries something it is not asking you to accept. That one carries the whole accusation. So what do I write? Refuse the question first. Then answer the one underneath it.

key: This sentence can be read two ways.

1.say: This sentence can be read two ways.

grammar.label: ambiguity as a tool and as a fault
grammar.form: constructive ambiguity in diplomacy and law; accidental ambiguity everywhere else
grammar.meaning: leaves two readings open, on purpose or by accident

explanation.en: Most ambiguity is a mistake. A little of it is the point: a treaty clause that both sides can sign, a line of verse that means two things at once. The C2 skill is telling them apart in your own drafts, which is hard because the writer always knows which reading was meant.
explanation.uz: Ko'p hollarda noaniqlik — xato. Ba'zan esa maqsad: ikkala tomon imzolay oladigan shartnoma bandi. Mahorat — o'z matningda ularni farqlash.

grammar.positive_example: The clause was left ambiguous so that both ministers could sign it.
grammar.negative_example: The clause was left ambiguous, which nobody noticed until the dispute.

l1_notes.uz: Ataylab qoldirilgan noaniqlik diplomatiyada vosita; tasodifiy noaniqlik esa doim xato.

grammar.label: presupposition and the loaded question
grammar.form: a question or statement whose framing smuggles in an unexamined claim
grammar.meaning: makes the reader accept something before they can consider it

explanation.en: 'When did the department stop keeping records?' presupposes that it did. You cannot answer without conceding. The defence is not to refuse to answer but to name the presupposition — 'I do not accept that it ever stopped' — and the offence is to notice when your own writing does it by accident.
explanation.uz: 'When did the department stop keeping records?' — to'xtaganini shart qilib oladi. Javob berish bilan roziliksiz roziliksan. Himoya — javob bermaslik emas, shartni nomlash.

grammar.positive_example: The question presupposes a decision that the minutes do not record.
grammar.negative_example: The question presupposes a decision, which is why I will not answer it.

l1_notes.uz: Savol ichiga yashiringan da'vo — ritorik vosita; uni sezish alohida ko'nikma.
